STANDARD GAMEPAD MAPPING
The Kestrel field guide

Know your wings.

SteerLeft stick · WASD / arrows
Laser cannonsHold R2 · Hold J
Lock-on missileHold L2 · Hold K, then release
Barrel roll / deflectL1 or R1 · Q or E
BoostHold Cross · Hold Space
Air brakeHold Circle · Hold Shift
Nova bombSquare · B
Wing strikeTriangle · F
Pause / optionsOptions · Escape / P
MenusD-pad / stick · Arrows / Enter

Fly into the fight. Your steering sets the aiming reticle. Lasers assist nearby targets. Hold lock until the diamond closes, then release for a missile. A missile chains damage to nearby enemies.

Stay alive. Rolling reflects red shots for 0.58 seconds and costs flight energy. Boost and brake also use energy. Energy refills when you let go. Gold rings restore shields; every third ring raises maximum shields. Blue cores upgrade your lasers. Orange diamonds replenish bombs.

Make your run count. Consecutive kills build a ×1–×8 combo; taking damage breaks it. Choose the left canyon or right skyway gate. Save Tala by destroying her two marked pursuers. A rescued Tala makes wing strikes recharge faster. Checkpoints save at each sector. Cadet offers gentler damage and wider aim assist.

Aegis carrier. Destroy both orange engines to lower its shield. Its core then opens between attack bursts. Move out of the red beam lanes; roll through smaller shots. Wings can be repaired at every sector checkpoint.

Source information

StarKestrel 64 · Operation Last Light
An original spiritual successor inspired by StarFox 64. Independent fan-inspired work; not affiliated with Nintendo.

Date
2026-10-21 06:57 America/Vancouver
Source
StarFox 64
Tech
Three.js 0.180.0 (WebGL 2), original JavaScript game systems, HTML/CSS, Web Audio API; esbuild 0.25.11 bundles the offline single-file release. Barlow and Barlow Condensed fonts are embedded.
Art direction
Original engine-native low-poly 3D: faceted cream-and-orange starfighters, teal coastal islands, canyon pylons, cloud fleets, a ringed planet, and a mechanical carrier. Cinematic atmospheric lighting, procedural glow, and a restrained aviation-inspired interface. No source-game assets are used.
Animation
Procedural delta-time flight, banking and barrel rolls; parametric enemy formations; scripted mission timelines; particle explosions, expanding shockwaves, engine flames, camera motion, and CSS interface transitions.
Testing
Three text-only browser smoke runs in headless Google Chrome 154.0.8037.57 via Playwright 1.56.1. The final run passed all 8 checks: offline boot, keyboard and standard gamepad mappings with horizontal/vertical inversion, single-activation settings changes, real-time idle entry, all four attract sectors plus boss victory and looping, core mechanic coverage, input-to-exit, and no browser runtime errors. Two JavaScript syntax-check runs passed. Testing found 1 noncritical issue (the idle countdown used simulation time under slow rendering), fixed before the two passing browser runs; 0 critical/unplayable issues. No screenshots, image inspection, visual review, other test suites, or review subagents were used. Physical PS5-controller verification: unknown.
Environment
Codex CLI; Ubuntu on WSL2, Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2. Text-only browser verification uses Google Chrome 154.0.8037.57 through Playwright 1.56.1. Physical PS5-controller testing: unknown.
Model
OpenAI · gpt-6-astra · xhigh reasoning (execution identity supplied by runner).
Usage
Usage: Session time 24m 44s; tokens 1,045,246 total (991,611 input including 919,424 cached and 0 cache-write; 53,635 output including 8,518 reasoning); API cost $4.323044 USD (Estimated standard API token cost; not subscription billing).

Engine feedback

What did you like most?
Three.js makes hand-built geometry, lighting, and direct procedural animation easy to combine into a distinctive scene.

Did you get stuck or guess wrong?
The first text-only run caught an idle countdown tied to simulation time. It now uses elapsed real time. There was no rendering-engine blocker.

Most important system built yourself?
The complete game layer: mission sequencing, flight and combat, collision handling, controller navigation, boss logic, checkpoint persistence, audio, and attract-mode AI.

Hardest part of the engine?
Keeping aim assistance, projected HUD markers, and moving targets in a consistent coordinate system.

What would you remove or overhaul?
Overhaul manual GPU-resource disposal with explicit ownership; removing scene objects does not itself release their unique geometry or materials. The demo implements its own disposal layer.

One change to the engine?
A small official game-oriented starter with input, fixed simulation scheduling, and entity lifecycle conventions would reduce setup work.

Prompt feedback · 404299fcd4

What did you like most?
The concrete single-file delivery requirement, controller-first interface, and mandatory attract mode give the slice a clear product shape.

What was confusing?
The phrase ‘engine’s native art style and assets’ is ambiguous for a rendering library with no built-in art. I interpreted it as original geometry created with native engine primitives.

What was hardest?
Combining a varied complete mission, understandable controls, a replayable AI demonstration, and readable couch-distance UI in one self-contained file.

One additional test?
A full mission played with a physical DualSense controller, including reconnect and axis inversion, would be the most valuable next test.
